raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm an old hand at this — been working these 9 mu for 40 years, same wheat-maize rotation my whole life.

---

**My thinking, in my own voice:**

This year I'll do the same as usual — wheat in the fall, maize right after. My whole 9 mu goes into both crops, that's just how we do it around here. No point in changing a system that's fed my family for decades.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10-12, same time as everyone in the village. I buy seed every couple of years from the supply station — this year I'll buy fresh "Jimai 22" or whatever they have, about 30 yuan per mu worth. I put down a bag of compound fertilizer (45% NPK, 15-15-15) before plowing — that's about 40 kg per mu, gives me around 6 kg N base. Then at jointing in March I topdress urea, maybe 20-25 kg per mu, so my total N ends up around 16-17 kg/mu. The extension fellow tells us 15 is enough but I've always done a bit more — when wheat looks yellow it worries me and I'd rather spend the extra 30 yuan than see a thin field. Irrigate 3 times usually — winter water before freeze, then return-green in March, and jointing. If May is dry I'll add a filling irrigation. Well water costs me about 40-50 yuan per mu each time, adds up.

For maize, the tight turnaround is the hard part. I harvest wheat around June 8-10, then I hire the combine and the no-till planter fellow comes through right after — costs about 40 yuan per mu combined but I've got no time or back left to do it by hand. Seed I buy every year, hybrid "Zhengdan 958" type, around 50 yuan per mu. Fertilizer — one application of compound at planting, about 30-35 kg per mu, then urea topdress at big-flare stage if the leaves look pale, maybe 15 kg. Total N around 13-15 kg/mu. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — if July-August rains come I don't irrigate at all, if dry I'll water once or twice. Harvest late September, early October.

Pesticide: herbicide on both crops for sure — weeds are worse than they used to be. Maybe one insecticide spray on maize if I see armyworms. I don't spray much — costs money and my eyes aren't what they were for mixing chemicals.

Labor: my wife and I do most of it, my oldest son comes back for busy seasons (harvest and planting), the younger ones have off-farm jobs. I hire machinery operators for combine harvest and planting — at my age I can't do it all by hand anymore.

Expected yields: last year wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, maize around 520. I expect similar this year if the weather behaves.
